forces: A remote peer controls response status, acknowledgment content, timing, and connection failure, so acceptance must be exact, bounded, and fail closed.
The Node binding must prove delivery semantics without acquiring an unapproved socket, HTTP client, host fetch, credential, or third-party runtime dependency.
Attempt identity must preserve canonical event identity without mutating caller-owned event data or implying retry, durability, or exactly-once behavior.
Serialized request bytes and peer-controlled diagnostics must remain bounded and secret-free while result classes stay deterministic for conformance tests.
